source_text: ἐπιστέλλοντι· «ἐσεβάσθησαν καὶ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα». 34.11 Τοῦτο δὲ τοῦ νομοθετήσαντος Μωυσέως· «ὁ θυσιάζων θεοῖς ἀλλοτρίοις λιθοβοληθήσεται, πλὴν κυρίῳ μόνῳ». 34.12 πρόσφατος δὲ καὶ ἀλλότριος θεὸς ὁ μὴ ὁμοούσιος τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ ὢν καὶ ποτὲ μὴ ὑπάρξας. 34.13 Καὶ οἱ λέγοντες «δόξα πατρὶ δι' υἱοῦ ἐν ἁγίῳ πνεύματι» οὐ δοξάζουσι τὸν υἱὸν ἢ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ. 34.14 ἄλλῳ γὰρ δι' ἄλλου ἐν ἄλλῳ ἀναπέμπουσι τὴν δόξαν, μᾶλλον δὲ οὐδ' ὁποτέρῳ. 34.15 καὶ παρατιτρώσκουσι τοῦτο μὲν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρὸς λέγοντος· «τὴν δόξαν μου ἑτέρῳ οὐ δώσω» ἀντὶ τοῦ ἑτεροφυεῖ οὐ δώσω, βουλομένου δὲ τιμᾶσθαι τὸν υἱὸν ὁμοίως αὐτοῦ, τοῦτο δὲ καὶ τὴν παράδοσιν τοῦ υἱοῦ, 34.16 ὅμοια πάσχοντες τῶν Χριστὸν μὲν αὐτὸν τῷ στόματι καλούντων, ταῖς δὲ χερσὶ τυπτόντων καὶ κραζόντων· «προφήτευσον ἡμῖν, Χριστέ, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;» τῶν καὶ λεγόντων οὕτως· «πιστεύομεν ὡς Μωϋσῆς καὶ οἱ προφῆται», αὐτὸν δὲ τὸν προφητευθέντα σταυρωσάντων. 34.17 Ὅτε οὖν καὶ ὁ θεὸς πατὴρ σὺν τῷ μονογενεῖ θεῷ παρακούεται καὶ ἡ εἰς κτίσμα πίστις ἀνωφελής ἐστιν, βλάπτειν μᾶλλον ἢ σώζειν δυναμένη, αὐτοὶ λογιζέσθωσαν, εἰ ἀκίνδυνον ἔχουσι πίστιν τὴν σωτηρίαν ἀρνούμενοι· δεῖ γὰρ σωθῆναι ὀρθῶς πιστεύοντα· καλὸν γάρ, φασί, τὸ σωθῆναι, τἄλλα δέ ἐστιν ἄλλος λόγος. 34.18 Καὶ Μακεδονίου δὲ παῖδες ὡς τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος οὕτω καὶ τοῦ μονογενοῦς τὴν δόξαν οὐ σώζουσιν ὁμοιούσιον τῷ πατρὶ καὶ οὐχὶ ὁμοούσιον λέγοντες αὐτὸν ὡς νοεῖσθαι, ὅτι ἄλλης ὁμοίας οὐσίας ἐστίν. 34.19 Ὥστε λείπεται αἱρετικοὺς ἢ ἀμεῖψαι ἐν ταῖς θρησκείαις αὐτῶν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς ὡς τῇ ἀληθείᾳ παρ' αὐτοῖς οὐκ ὄντος πατρός, ἔτι μὴν καὶ τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ, καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος δὲ τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς τοῦτο οὐκ ὄντος–συγγνώτω δὲ ἡμῖν ἡ ἁγία καὶ σεπτὴ καὶ παρ' ἡμῶν δοξαζομένη ὁμοούσιος τριάς–, ἀμεῖψαι δὲ πρό γε πάντων τὸ ἑαυτῶν ὄνομα καὶ μήτε καλεῖσθαι Χριστιανοὺς ἢ πνευματικούς, μήτε διακεῖσθαι ὡς ὄντες αὐτοὶ ἐκεῖνοι ὁμογενεῖς υἱοὶ τῶν ἰδίων πατέρων, ἢ μὴ ἐξαλλάττειν τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς θεότητος καὶ δόξης τὸν ἀληθινὸν υἱὸν καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ. 34.20 ἴδιον γὰρ Ἰουδαίων μὲν τὸ τὸν πατέρα μόνον τιμᾷν, Ἑλλήνων δὲ τὸ πλῆθος δαιμονίων μέγα καὶ μικρὸν καὶ χρονικὸν καὶ ἑτεροούσιον σέβειν. 35.ν Ὅπως χρὴ νοεῖν τὰς θεολογίας τῶν γραφῶν. 35.1 Συναγωνίσασθαι δὲ ὁ ἀνάξιος ἐγὼ ταῖς περὶ τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος θεολογίαις προήχθην οὐδὲ κατὰ ἔννοιαν παραβλάπτων τὴν περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἄφραστον δόξαν–οὐ γὰρ ἠγνόηται, ὡς εἰ καὶ μὴ πρὸ ἀμφοῖν δεδήλωται τῶν εἰρημένων θείων ὑποστάσεων, ἀλλ' ὅμως ἄμφω αἱ ὑποστάσεις ἐξ αὐτοῦ κατὰ φύσιν συμφυῶς εἰσιν, ἡ μὲν τοῦ υἱοῦ γεννητικῶς, ἡ δὲ τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ ἐκπορευτικῶς–, ἀλλ' αἱρετικῶν τὰς πανολεθρίους ἐξηγήσεις ἀποσκευαζόμενος καὶ συνιστάμενος, ὅδι δι' ὧν δοκοῦσι παρὰ τὴν γραφὴν πλέον 40 τιμᾶν τὸν πατέρα, διὰ τούτων αὐτόν τε λυποῦσι καὶ τὸν μονογενῆ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα ἐνυβρίζουσιν. 36.ν Καὶ τοῦτο περὶ τοῦ αὐτοῦ. 36.1 Τοὺς τοίνυν ὀρθοδόξους χρὴ εἰδέναι μέν, ὡς καὶ περὶ μικροῦ ἔργου τοῦ θεοῦ–εἰ τολμήσαντα μικρὸν ἔργον ἔστι φάναι θεοῦ–τοῖς διαλαβεῖν ἐθέλουσι χρεία λόγων, καὶ ἔργων πρὸ τῶν λόγων, καὶ πίστεως πρὸ ἀμφοῖν τούτων, καὶ πολλῆς εὐλαβείας καὶ κατανοήσεως ἀκροτάτης, ἵνα διὰ ταῦτα γνῶναι ἀξιωθέντες, ὡς καὶ τὸ μικρὸν οὐχ ἁλώσιμον τῇ διανοίᾳ, ἀλλ' ἀπείρως καὶ αὐτὸ τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων ὑπερφέρει ἐπιβολῶν–εἰ γὰρ τοῦ θεοῦ ἔργον, κἂν μικρὸν δοκῇ, μέγα ὡς θεοῦ· «μικροῖς δὲ τὰ μεγάλα πῶς ἕλοι τις ἂν πόνοισιν; ἀμαθές», φασίν, «καὶ τὸ βούλεσθαι τάδε»–, πολλῷ δὲ μᾶλλον ἡ περὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἀφράστου θεοῦ διάληψις ὑπερβαίνουσα καὶ ἀρχαγγέλων αἴσθησιν τῶν μὲν σφαλερῶν ζητήσεων ἀναχωρήσωσινʹ, γινώσκειν αὐτὰ μόνῳ τῷ θεῷ ἀφιέντες, σὺν τῷ ἀποστόλῳ δὲ εἴπωσιν· «ἐπίστευσα, διὸ καὶ ἐλάλησα»· 36.2 τὰς δὲ θεολογίας τῶν γραφῶν νοεῖν οὑτωσί, ὅτιπερ, ὅταν ἀπὸ ἑνὸς προσώπου λέγουσιν, διὰ τὴν μίαν φύσιν καὶ θέλησιν· ὅταν ἀπὸ ἀμφοῖν, διὰ τὸ δείκνυσθαι τὸ ἰδιοσύστατον τῆς ἁγίας καὶ ἀκηράτου τριάδος· 36.3 ὅταν γὰρ Ἠσαΐας λέγῃ· «ἐγὼ κύριος ἐξέτεινα τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐστερέωσα τὴν γῆν» καὶ πάλιν· «ἐγώ εἰμι καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλος θεὸς πλὴν ἐμοῦ», διὰ τὴν μίαν θεότητα καὶ συμφωνίαν, ὡς προείρηται· 36.4 ὅταν δόξῃ μὴ μνημονεύεσθαι τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, διὰ τὸ συμπεριέχεσθαι αὐτὸ τῷ θεῷ, οὗ πνεῦμα τυγχάνει ὄν· ὅταν τὴν μυσταγωγίαν
pass_a_gloss: [...to the Romans] writing: 'they revered and served the creation beside the one who created'. 34.11 And this of Moses who gave the law: 'the one sacrificing to foreign gods will be stoned, except to the Lord alone'. 34.12 And a fresh and foreign god is the one not being of the same being with God and Father and at some time not having been. 34.13 And the ones saying 'glory to the Father through the Son in the Holy Spirit' do not glorify the Son or the Spirit of God. 34.14 For to one through another in another they send up the glory, or rather to neither one. 34.15 And they wound on the one hand the will of the Father who says: 'my glory to another I will not give', in place of: to one of another nature I will not give, and who wishes the Son to be honoured likewise with himself; and on the other also the handing-down of the Son, 34.16 suffering things like those calling him Christ with the mouth but striking with the hands and shouting: 'prophesy to us, Christ, who is the one who hit you?', those also saying thus: 'we believe as Moses and the prophets', but crucifying the very one prophesied. 34.17 When then also God the Father together with the only-begotten God is not listened to and the faith into a creature is unprofitable, able to harm rather than save, let them reckon for themselves whether they have a faith without danger while denying the salvation; for it is needful to be saved believing rightly; for a fine thing, they say, is the being saved, and the other things are another account. 34.18 And the children of Macedonius, as of the Holy Spirit, so also of the only-begotten do not keep safe the glory, saying him like-in-being to the Father and not same-in-being, so as to be thought that he is of another, similar being. 34.19 So that it is left for heretics either to exchange in their acts of worship the name of the Father, as with them not being Father in truth, and further indeed also that of the only-begotten Son, and that of the Spirit of God, as this not being so (and may the holy and venerable Trinity, glorified by us, of the same being, pardon us), and before all to exchange their own name and neither be called Christians or spiritual, nor be disposed as being themselves sons of the same kind as their own fathers; or not to alienate from the Father's deity and glory the true Son and his Holy Spirit. 34.20 For it is proper to Jews to honour the Father alone, and to Greeks to revere the crowd of demons, great and small and time-bound and of another being. 35.ν [Chapter title:] How one must understand the theologies of the writings. 35.1 And I, the unworthy one, was led forward to contend alongside the theologies about the only-begotten Son and the Holy Spirit, not even in thought damaging the unspeakable glory about God and Father (for it is not unknown that, even if he has not been made plain before both of the said divine hypostases, yet both the hypostases are from him according to nature, growing together, the one of the Son by way of begetting, the other of his Spirit by way of proceeding), but packing away the all-destructive explanations of heretics and establishing this: that through the things by which they seem to honour the Father more than the writing does, through these they both grieve him and insult his only-begotten and the Spirit. 36.ν [Chapter title:] And this about the same thing. 36.1 The right-believing then must know, on the one hand, that even about a small work of God (if having dared it is possible to say a small work of God) for those wishing to grasp it there is need of words, and of works before the words, and of faith before both of these, and of much reverence and of the highest consideration, so that, through these having been deemed worthy to know that even the small is not catchable by the thinking, but endlessly it too surpasses human attempts (for if a work of God, even if it seems small, it is great as God's: 'and how would anyone seize the great things with small toils? unlearned', they say, 'is even the wishing for these'), and much more the grasp about the unspeakable God himself, going beyond even the perception of archangels, they may draw back from slippery searchings, leaving it to God alone to know them, and say with the apostle: 'I believed, therefore also I spoke'; 36.2 and to understand the theologies of pass_b_english: … writing: “They worshipped and served the creature rather than the Creator” (Romans 1:25). And they transgress this command of Moses the lawgiver: “Whoever sacrifices to foreign gods, and not to the Lord alone, shall be stoned” (Exodus 22:20). Now a new and foreign god is one who is not consubstantial with God the Father and who once did not exist.

And those who say, “Glory to the Father through the Son in the Holy Spirit,” do not glorify the Son or the Spirit of God. For they send up the glory to one, through another, in another; or rather, to neither. And they do injury both to the will of the Father, who says, “My glory I will not give to another” (Isaiah 42:8), meaning to one of another nature, and who wills that the Son be honoured as he is (John 5:23), and to the tradition handed down by the Son. They fare like those who called him Christ with their mouths but struck him with their hands and cried out, “Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?” (Matthew 26:68); the same who said, “We believe as Moses and the prophets did,” and yet crucified the very one who had been prophesied.

Since, then, God the Father too goes unheeded together with the only-begotten God, and faith in a creature is useless, able to harm rather than to save, let them consider for themselves whether their faith is free of danger while they deny salvation. For a person must be saved by believing rightly. To be saved is a fine thing, as they say; the rest is another story.

The children of Macedonius, too, do not keep the glory of the Only-begotten, any more than that of the Holy Spirit. They call him of like substance with the Father, and not of the same substance, so that he is understood to be of another substance, a similar one.

So the heretics are left with this choice. Either they must change, in their worship, the name of the Father, since among them he is not truly Father; and that of the only-begotten Son as well; and that of the Spirit of God too, as not being that either (may the holy, venerable and consubstantial Trinity, whom we glorify, pardon us for saying it!). And above all they must change their own name, and no longer be called Christians or spiritual, nor count themselves sons of one kind with their own fathers. Or else they must not estrange the true Son and his Holy Spirit from the Father’s Godhead and glory. For it is the mark of Jews to honour the Father alone, and of Greeks to worship a multitude of demons, great and small, bound by time and of other substances.
How the theology of the Scriptures is to be understood.

I, unworthy as I am, was drawn to take up the cause of the theology of the only-begotten Son and the Holy Spirit, without impairing, even in thought, the ineffable glory of God the Father. For it is well known that, even if he has not been set forth here ahead of both the divine hypostases just named, both hypostases are nevertheless from him by nature and as one in nature with him: that of the Son by way of begetting, that of his Spirit by way of procession. Rather, I was clearing away the ruinous interpretations of the heretics and showing this: that by the very means through which they seem to honour the Father more than Scripture does, they grieve him and outrage his Only-begotten and the Spirit.

The orthodox, then, must know this. Even about a small work of God (if one may dare to call any work of God small), those who wish to treat it need words; and works before words; and faith before both of these; and much reverence and the most searching reflection. All this so that, counted worthy through these things to know that even the small thing cannot be captured by the mind, but itself surpasses human efforts of thought without limit (for if it is God’s work, even if it seems small, it is great, as being God’s: “How could anyone take great things with small labours? It is foolish,” they say, “even to want it”), and that much more does the comprehension of the ineffable God himself surpass even the perception of archangels, they may withdraw from perilous inquiries, leaving the knowledge of these things to God alone, and say with the apostle: “I believed, and therefore I spoke” (2 Corinthians 4:13).

And they must understand the theology of the Scriptures in this way. When the Scriptures speak from one person, it is because of the one nature and will; when from both, it is to show the distinct subsistence of the holy and pure Trinity. So when Isaiah says, “I the Lord stretched out the heaven and made firm the earth” (Isaiah 44:24), and again, “I am, and there is no other God besides me” (Isaiah 45:5), it is because of the one Godhead and concord, as was said before. choices.issue: Paragraphs dropped, opening fragment, negated sentence
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English began with the stray fragment 'instead of the Creator' (the end of Romans 1:25) and then jumped to 34.20, dropping edition paragraphs 34.11-34.19 entirely: Moses' law against sacrifice to foreign gods, the 'new god' defined, the doxology 'Glory to the Father through the Son in the Holy Spirit' and its fault, the comparison with those who mocked Christ, the warning on faith in a creature, the followers of Macedonius, and the heretics' dilemma. All restored, and Romans 1:25 given whole. In 36.2 the old English said the theology of the Scriptures is 'not to be understood in this way'; the Greek says it is to be understood so. Also fixed: 'contended with' (συναγωνίσασθαι: fought alongside), 'preparing and setting forth' (ἀποσκευαζόμενος: clearing away), 'those who wish to engage with the orthodox' (the orthodox must know), 'understanding of the listener' (the keenest reflection), 'the Holy Spirit is not mentioned in glory' (δόξῃ: seems), 'as it is foretold' (as was said before). Wrong references: 'Isa 40:22' for the stretching of the heaven (Isaiah 44:24, Greek wording), 'Isa 44:6' made Isaiah 45:5 (nearest wording). Added: Romans 1:25, Exodus 22:20, Isaiah 42:8, John 5:23, Matthew 26:68. Bracket fillers [I am] and [Son] removed. Chapter titles 35.ν and 36.ν stand as their own paragraphs.

choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence ('and in Paul, to the Romans' ends the previous section). Only this section's words are translated, with a leading ellipsis.

choices.english: And they transgress this command of Moses the lawgiver
choices.why: Continues the list of commands the heretics transgress (34.6-34.10); 'they transgress' is carried over, not added.

choices.term: ἄλλῳ γὰρ δι' ἄλλου ἐν ἄλλῳ ἀναπέμπουσι τὴν δόξαν
choices.english: they send up the glory to one, through another, in another
choices.why: Kept in Didymus' clipped form: the prepositions rank the Son and Spirit below the Father, so the glory reaches only one.
Didymus' idiom for the followers of Macedonius; kept.

choices.english: of like substance … not of the same substance
choices.why: The technical pair is put in English; 'consubstantial' is used where ὁμοούσιος stands alone (34.12, 34.19).

choices.term: μήτε διακεῖσθαι ὡς ὄντες αὐτοὶ ἐκεῖνοι ὁμογενεῖς υἱοὶ τῶν ἰδίων πατέρων
choices.english: nor count themselves sons of one kind with their own fathers
choices.why: Didymus' jibe: those who deny that the Son is of the Father's kind should not claim to be of one kind with their own fathers.

choices.term: καλὸν γάρ, φασί, τὸ σωθῆναι, τἄλλα δέ ἐστιν ἄλλος λόγος
choices.english: To be saved is a fine thing, as they say; the rest is another story
choices.why: A proverb ('φασί'); rendered as an English saying.

choices.term: μικροῖς δὲ τὰ μεγάλα πῶς ἕλοι τις ἂν πόνοισιν; ἀμαθές … καὶ τὸ βούλεσθαι τάδε
choices.english: “How could anyone take great things with small labours? It is foolish,” they say, “even to want it”
choices.why: A verse quotation (iambic, with the poetic form πόνοισιν) introduced by 'they say'; translated as quoted, source not named in the reading text.

choices.term: οὐ γὰρ ἠγνόηται, ὡς εἰ καὶ μὴ πρὸ ἀμφοῖν δεδήλωται
choices.english: it is well known that, even if he has not been set forth here ahead of both
choices.why: Didymus explains why his treatise took the Son and Spirit before the Father; 'here' makes the reference to the treatise plain without a bracket.

choices.term: ταῖς … θεολογίαις / τὰς θεολογίας τῶν γραφῶν
choices.english: the theology of … / the theology of the Scriptures
choices.why: θεολογία in Didymus is speaking of someone as God; English 'theology' keeps the term the chapter title uses.
